title: Purity for regular closed immersions
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion of pure codimension
$c$, with $X$ smooth over the perfect field $k$ and $Z$ regular.

*The fundamental class.* A *frame* of $Z$ is an étale
$U\to X$ together with $f_1,\dots,f_c\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ generating
the ideal of $Z_U=Z\times_XU$. Each $f_j$ is a unit on $U\setminus V(f_j)$,
so it has a Kummer class $\kappa(f_j)\in H^1(U\setminus V(f_j),\Lambda(1))$
as in [sk-def-purity-conv], and the boundary of the localization sequence
of $V(f_j)\subset U$ gives
$\partial\kappa(f_j)\in H^2_{V(f_j)}(U,\Lambda(1))$. The *class of
the frame* is the cup product with supports

$$
\operatorname{cl}(f)=\partial\kappa(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(f_c)
\ \in\ H^{2c}_{Z_U}\bigl(U,\Lambda(c)\bigr).
$$

Then:
- **(a)** $Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ with
$\mathcal H^0$ free of rank one; hence
$H^0(Z,Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c])=H^{2c}_Z(X,\Lambda(c))=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal H^0)$,
and likewise after any étale $U\to X$.
- **(b)** $\operatorname{cl}(f)$ depends only on $Z_U\subset U$, not on
the frame, and the frame classes glue to a unique global class, the
*fundamental class*

$$
[Z\subset X]=\operatorname{cl}_{Z/X}\ \in\ H^{2c}_Z\bigl(X,\Lambda(c)\bigr)
=H^0\bigl(Z,Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c]\bigr),
$$

which generates $\mathcal H^0$ at every geometric point. (The frame
classes and their gluing make sense for every regular closed immersion;
for the zero section of $\Aaf^1_Y$ the class so defined is
$\mathrm{pur}_s$ of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] with $c=1$, and for the zero section of $\Aaf^c_B$
it is the generator $\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$
of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity], by the definition of those classes; these pairs are
in the situation of the theorem when $Y$, resp. $B$, is smooth over $k$.)
- **(c)** The morphism

$$
\operatorname{cl}_i:\ \Lambda_Z\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c],
\qquad 1\longmapsto[Z\subset X],
$$

is an isomorphism, and it equals the isomorphism assembled from smooth
purity of $a_X$ and $a_Z$ in Steps 1–2 below. Since twists pass through
$Ri^{!}$ ([sk-lem-coprojection]), equivalently the inverse of
$\operatorname{cl}_i(-c)[-2c]$ is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Ri^{!}\Lambda_X\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c].
$$

- **(d)** It is compatible with étale base change,
$[Z_U\subset U]=[Z\subset X]|_U$, and with exterior products: for two such
pairs $(X_1,Z_1)$, $(X_2,Z_2)$ over $k$, the product
$(X_1\times_kX_2,Z_1\times_kZ_2)$ is again such a pair, of codimension
$c_1+c_2$, and
$[Z_1\times Z_2\subset X_1\times X_2]=[Z_1\subset X_1]\boxtimes[Z_2\subset X_2]$
under the exterior product of classes with supports.

proof.text:
*Step 1: the dualizing-object identification.* Work in the finite-coefficient, separated finite-type setting of [sk-def-purity-conv]. Components of $X$ disjoint from $Z$ contribute the zero category and need no dimension subtraction. On every other connected component, [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure] gives smooth $a_X$ and $a_Z=a_Xi$ of pure dimensions $n$ and $m=n-c$. The exceptional composition comparison for $i$, which need not be smooth, is obtained formally from [thm-sf-comp-composition] and the adjunctions of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: for every bounded constructible $M$ and $L$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,R(a_Xi)^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(a_Xi)_!M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{X!}Ri_!M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Ri^!Ra_X^!L).$$
Yoneda gives $c_{a_X,i}:Ra_Z^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!Ra_X^!$; the identity and associativity clauses of the compact-support theorem give those of this comparison. Write $\Pi_f:\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(d)[2d]$ for the specified diagonal orientation of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]. In the notation of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], $\Pi_f^{-1}=\gamma_{f,\Lambda}$ after the unit identifications. Thus $\omega_Z\cong Ri^!\omega_X$, $\omega_X\cong\Lambda_X(n)[2n]$ and $\omega_Z\cong\Lambda_Z(m)[2m]$. The identifications assemble over the disjoint components.

source.place: Step 1; expanded using the cited current DAG statements

proof.text: *Step 2a: cancel the twist.* Apply [lem-pur-twist-cancellation] to the data $b=c_{a_X,i}$, $\Pi_X=\Pi_{a_X}$ and $\Pi_Z=\Pi_{a_Z}$ from Step 1, on each component meeting $Z$. Its dimension equality is $n=m+c$. The co-projection hypotheses [lem-pur-coprojection] hold: $\Lambda_X$ is bounded constructible and the Tate shifts $\Lambda_X(n)[2n]$, $\Lambda_X(-m)[-2m]$ are bounded constructible finite-Tor invertible objects. Denote the specified composite by $\Phi_i$; it is exactly [pur9-rg-def-phi], with direction $\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!(\Lambda_X(c)[2c])$. Hence the target is a degree-zero sheaf free of rank one, and cancellation also gives $Ri^!\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]$.

source.place: Step 2, twist cancellation and the direction of Phi_i

proof.text: *Step 2b: identify supported cohomology.* For $F=\Lambda_X(c)$, [lem-pur-supported-hom] gives $H_Z^{2c}(X,F)=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*\Lambda_Z,F[2c])$. The closed compactification $(\operatorname{id}_Z,i)$ gives $i_*=Ri_!=Ri_*$ [prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit], so the bounded constructible adjunction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_Z,Ri^!(F[2c]))=H^0(Z,Ri^!(F[2c]))$. Both inputs are bounded constructible and finite-Tor. Step 2a identifies the latter group with sections of the degree-zero sheaf. For an etale neighbourhood $u:U\to X$, the pullback $v:Z\times_XU\to Z$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] (apply it to $(u,\operatorname{id}_X)$). Smoothness and dimensions persist by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. The etale local ring maps are flat [def-weil-etale-morphism]; tensoring each injective multiplication map for a regular sequence preserves injectivity, and its quotient at a point of $Z\times_XU$ is nonzero. Thus the same cancellation and adjunction argument applies there. This proves (a), including its etale-local assertion.

source.place: Step 2, supported cohomology and etale neighbourhoods

proof.text: *Step 3: define the fundamental class.* For every frame, [def-pur-frame-class] defines the supported Kummer-boundary cup product, with the empty-frame unit when $c=0$. By [lem-pur-frame-independence] two frames of the same closed pair give the same class. Its hypotheses hold for every frame $u:U\to X$: $X$ and $Z$ are smooth over $k$ by [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure], so $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Z_U\to Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] (the etale maps having relative dimension $0$); the relative dimension of $U$ over $k$ is locally constant, so one applies the definition and the lemma on each of the finitely many open and closed pieces of $U$ of constant relative dimension, the class on $U$ being the family of these classes; and $Z_U$ has pure codimension $c$ in $U$, since by Step 2 its ideal is generated near each point by a regular sequence of length $c$, and dividing a Noetherian local ring by a regular sequence lowers its dimension by the length of the sequence. Under Step 2 these are sections of the degree-zero sheaf on $Z$. Here restriction is the restriction of supported classes: the localization boundaries are functorial by [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], and the supported-Hom construction in [lem-pur-supported-hom] commutes with restricting the closed-open pair. Frames exist Zariski-locally by the definition of regular immersion in [sk-def-purity-conv]. Pulling the frames to an overlap gives frames of the same pair, whose classes agree by frame independence; the sheaf axiom therefore glues them to a unique global section $[Z\subset X]$.

source.place: Step 3; expanded using the cited current DAG statements

proof.text:
*Step 4a: etale locality of the specified orientation.* Let $u:U\to X$ be an etale neighbourhood, with $V=Z\times_XU$, $v:V\to Z$ and $i_U:V\hookrightarrow U$. Take finite-type separated neighbourhoods; all pairs are then in the finite-coefficient exceptional-functor setting. By [lem-pur-etale-orientation-locality] the adjunction-preserving restriction comparison
$$B_{u,i}:Ri_U^!Lu^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lv^*Ri^!$$
satisfies $B_{u,i}\Phi_{i_U}=Lv^*\Phi_i$, including the Tate shifts. This lemma includes agreement of the etale adjoint identification with the rank-zero diagonal orientation, so the restriction here is the specified one. Thus comparison of $\Phi_i(1)$ with the glued frame class can be checked on these neighbourhoods.

source.place: Step 4(i)-(ii), etale restriction and the normalized orientation

proof.text: *Step 4b: choose coordinates.* For $c\geq1$, [lem-pur-regular-immersion-linearization] supplies around every $z\in Z$ an etale $w:U\to\mathbf A^{c+m}_k$ with $V=Z\times_XU=w^{-1}(\mathbf A^m_k)$ scheme-theoretically, and with $w|_V$ etale. This is a pullback of the coordinate pair, not an isomorphism of $U$ with affine space. The functions $f_j=w^*t_j$ form a frame. By Step 3 it suffices to compare this frame with $\Phi_{i_U}(1)$, and Step 4a also applies to this pullback chart.

source.place: Step 4, etale linearization and reduction to the coordinate pair

proof.text:
*Step 4c: the coordinate normalization.* Put $p:\mathbf A^c_{\mathbf A^m}\to\mathbf A^m$, with zero section $i_0$. In the composite of Step 2a, substitute $a_{\mathbf A^{c+m}}=a_{\mathbf A^m}p$ and $pi_0=\operatorname{id}$. The smooth composition formula [thm-pur-composition-coherence] cancels the two occurrences of the orientation of $a_{\mathbf A^m}$, leaving $\Phi_{i_0}=T^{-1}$, where
$$T:Ri_0^!\Lambda(c)[2c]\xrightarrow{Ri_0^!\gamma_{p,\Lambda}}Ri_0^!Rp^!\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda.$$
By [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement], $\gamma_{p,\Lambda}$ is the ordered affine comparison. The normalization clause of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] therefore gives $\Phi_{i_0}=\mathrm{th}_c$ and $\Phi_{i_0}(1)=\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$. In particular this fixes the inverse direction, not just an unspecified rank-one isomorphism.

*Step 4d: pull back and glue the comparison.* Kummer classes commute with pullback [sk-def-purity-conv], as do localization boundaries [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. In the supported-Hom formula defining [def-pur-supported-cup], pullback tensors the pulled-back morphisms and their coefficient multiplication. Thus the class in Step 4c restricts to $\operatorname{cl}(w^*t_1,\ldots,w^*t_c)$ [def-pur-frame-class]. Step 4a identifies its associated morphism with $\Phi_{i_U}$. For $c=0$, locally the ideal is zero, so $i$ is the identity; its composite $\Phi_i$ cancels $\Pi_a^{-1}$ and $\Pi_a$ and is the identity, agreeing with the empty-frame unit. The charts cover $Z$, hence $\Phi_i(1)=[Z\subset X]$ globally. A map from $\Lambda_Z$ to a degree-zero sheaf is determined by the image of $1$, so $\operatorname{cl}_i=\Phi_i$. Its invertibility from Step 2a proves stalkwise generation and (b),(c).

source.place: Step 4(iv), pullback of the coordinate class and gluing; codimension zero

proof.text: *Step 5a: etale base change.* An etale base change pulls a frame back to a frame. Naturality of Kummer classes [sk-def-purity-conv], localization boundaries [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] and the tensor composite [def-pur-supported-cup] carries its class to that of the pulled-back frame. Step 3 and uniqueness of gluing give the asserted base-change identity. Since $\operatorname{cl}_i=\Phi_i$, Step 4a gives the same identity for the purity maps.

*Step 5b: the product is again a regular pair.* By [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure], $X_j$ and $Z_j$ are smooth over $k$. Base change and composition [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] give smoothness of both products; smooth algebras over a field have regular local rings [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local], so $Z_1\times_kZ_2$ is regular. Choose affine regular frames $f$ in $R$ and $g$ in $S$. By [lem-pur-product-regular-sequence] their concatenation in $R\otimes_kS$ is regular of length $c_1+c_2$, with quotient $R/(f)\otimes_kS/(g)$, the coordinate ring of the product closed subscheme. Such charts cover the product. This verifies regularity and pure codimension $c_1+c_2$ in the convention [sk-def-purity-conv], including empty sequences.

source.place: Step 5, regularity and codimension of the product

proof.text:
*Step 5c: the exterior-product identity.* On the product frames of Step 5b, [lem-pur-exterior-product-frame] identifies the concatenated frame class with $\operatorname{cl}(f)\boxtimes\operatorname{cl}(g)$ for the specified supported exterior product. Its hypotheses hold: all schemes are smooth on these constant-dimension components, both individual closed subschemes are smooth, and Step 5b gives the product codimension. By [lem-pur-frame-independence] and the uniqueness of gluing in Step 3, these local equalities give
$$[Z_1\times Z_2\subset X_1\times X_2]=[Z_1\subset X_1]\boxtimes[Z_2\subset X_2].$$
This proves (d).

source.place: Step 5, local supported exterior-product comparison and gluing
